title: Man with crushing central chest pain
stem: A 56 year old man presents two hours after the onset of crushing central chest pain radiating to the left arm, with sweating and nausea. He smokes and has treated hypertension.

history.q: Describe the pain and its onset.
history.a: Central, crushing, 9 of 10, began at rest two hours ago and has not eased.
Mild breathlessness since the pain began. No palpitations or syncope.
Smokes 15 cigarettes a day, hypertension on amlodipine, no diabetes. No allergies.
Two brief episodes of exertional chest tightness in the last month, each lasting five minutes.

exam.general: Anxious, pale and sweaty, comfortable only when sitting still.
exam.pulse: Regular pulse at 98 per minute, normal volume and character.
exam.precordium: Apex beat not displaced, normal character.

findings: ST elevation in V1 to V4 with hyperacute T waves
Reciprocal ST depression in II, III and aVF

echoTasks.find: Akinetic anterior septum and apex with preserved basal contraction

measure.what: Left ventricular ejection fraction by Simpson biplane

echoTasks.find: Akinetic anterior wall and apex in the left anterior descending territory

required.answer: Moderately impaired with ejection fraction 47 percent

diagnosis.answer: Acute anterior ST elevation myocardial infarction
accept: acute anterior st elevation myocardial infarction

management.model: Immediate reperfusion pathway with primary percutaneous coronary intervention, dual antiplatelet therapy and anticoagulation per protocol, analgesia, and monitoring for arrhythmia. Echocardiography must not delay reperfusion.
keyPoints: Activate the primary PCI pathway without delay
Give dual antiplatelet therapy and anticoagulation per protocol
Do not delay reperfusion for echocardiography

teaching: Anterior ST elevation with reciprocal depression localises to the left anterior descending artery.
A new regional wall motion abnormality appears within minutes of occlusion.
